$comment: flagstaff's capability matrix against the four packages it replaces (compat-oracle's LAYERS). Rendered by <CapabilityMatrix pkg="flagstaff" /> from apps/docs-chassis and held by scripts/capabilities-lock.test.ts: every `ours` yes/partial names a test file and a title substring it contains, or a compat-oracle grade; every incumbent cell names a source at the version compat-oracle grades, and a local source is checked for the text it `quote`s or `lacks`. `n/a` means the row does not apply to that package, and says why. A row that could not be proved for every column is not here.

rows.capability: One line per state change on a pipe
rows.why: A log file or an agent reading a pipe gets each state once, as text, instead of repainted frames or erase sequences.

ours.title: the static projection once per state change, no repaint

ora.missing: off an interactive terminal it writes the start line and the final line; text set in between is not written

log-update.note: writes erase sequences on every stream; its only isTTY check chooses synchronized output

boxen.note: returns one string; it has no states to change

cli-table3.note: returns one string; it has no states to change

rows.capability: A box that prints its text off a terminal
rows.why: Off a terminal the box component writes `title: text`, so a log or an agent reads the message rather than border characters.

ours.title: the component says the text off a terminal, and draws only on one

boxen.note: never checks the stream, so a pipe gets the same bordered drawing

rows.capability: A table that prints header-and-value pairs off a terminal
rows.why: Off a terminal each row is written as `header: value` pairs, which a log, an agent or a screen reader can read without the grid.

ours.title: the component emits header-and-value pairs off a terminal, not the grid

cli-table3.note: never checks the stream, so a pipe gets the same grid

rows.capability: A screen-reader mode, on a terminal too
rows.why: With `CLI_ACCESSIBLE=1` the output policy chooses the accessible mode ahead of the terminal check, so a component hoisted with `hoist()` prints its plain text once per state and never redraws; the `flagstaff/ora` drop-in keeps ora's behaviour instead.

ours.title: the mode is unchanged: accessible still decides redraws

boxen.note: draws the border for every reader

cli-table3.note: draws the grid for every reader

rows.capability: `--json`: one NDJSON event per state transition
rows.why: A component hoisted with `{ json: true }` writes each transition as a JSON object on stderr and leaves stdout for the result, so an agent parses state instead of scraping a terminal.

ours.title: json: one NDJSON event per transition on stderr, stdout untouched

rows.why: A test drives frames with `manualClock()` instead of patching global timers, so a spinner's terminal output is the same bytes on every run.

ours.title: the tty transcript is the same bytes twenty runs over

ora.note: frames are scheduled on the global timer

log-update.note: draws only when called; the caller owns the timing

rows.capability: A checker for plugins before they ship
rows.why: `npx flagstaff check ./plugin.mjs` renders every contribution in all five modes side by side, and exits 1 with a code and a fix on a refusal.

ours.title: prints the plugin in all five modes side by side and exits 0

rows.capability: Spinner, progress, tasks, box and table on one loop
rows.why: Every component is hoisted, updated and lowered the same way, and every one gets the same five output modes.

ours.title: writes no carriage return and no escape on a pipe

log-update.note: repaints whatever string it is given; it has no components

rows.capability: Custom styles through a validated plugin registry
rows.why: A spinner or border style is registered once, validated against the published JSON schema, and every component that draws one can use it by name.

ora.missing: a custom spinner object is passed to each instance; there is no registry and no schema

boxen.missing: a custom border object is passed to each call; there is no registry

cli-table3.missing: custom border characters are passed to each table; there is no registry and no validation

rows.capability: Every style must carry a text form
rows.why: A spinner or component without a static projection is refused at registration with `E_NO_STATIC_PROJECTION`, so nothing registered can only animate.

ours.title: a spinner without static: E_NO_STATIC_PROJECTION, with the fix

ora.note: a spinner is frames and an interval; nothing carries a text form

rows.capability: Cursor restored on SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP
rows.why: A spinner killed with Ctrl+C gives the cursor back and the process still terminates.

ours.title: puts the cursor back, and still terminates

rows.capability: Borders stay aligned around wide (CJK) characters
rows.why: Rows are measured in terminal columns, so a double-width character does not push a border out of line.

ours.title: a wide-character body still fits exactly

rows.capability: Every runtime dependency from the same repository
rows.why: Installing it adds closeout, linegauge, paratext and roundel, released from this repository through one pipeline, and nothing else.

ours.title: depends on closeout, linegauge, paratext and roundel and on nothing else

cli-table3.note: string-width, and @colors/colors as an optional dependency

rows.why: `flagstaff/ora` is graded by ora 9.4.1's own tests, unedited, so changing the import keeps ora's behaviour.

ora.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `flagstaff/log-update` is graded by log-update 8.0.0's own tests, which render every frame through a terminal emulator and assert the screen.

log-update.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `flagstaff/boxen` is graded by boxen 8.0.1's own tests, each a snapshot of the exact characters the box comes out as.

boxen.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `flagstaff/cli-table3` is graded by the cases of cli-table3 0.6.5's own suite that go through its public API.

cli-table3.note: its own suite, the control run
